frame_16ab1de91003.question: Vulnerability analysis of Pool
artifact_refs: Reserve-based swap pricing and whether spot reserves can be manipulated within or across transactions
Balance-delta swap input accounting and unsolicited token transfers affecting quoted prices
LP redemption pricing and interactions between pool reserves, balances, and share supply
Cross-pool pricing assumptions that may enable flash-loan or donation-based price distortion

history.rationale: WHY NOW: Pool is the core pricing component, and the graph explicitly identifies reserve-based swap pricing, balance-delta inputs, and reserve-based LP redemption as central behaviors. These mechanisms are the highest-priority surface for determining whether an attacker can manipulate spot prices through transient trades, token donations, or reserve/balance desynchronization and then extract value through swaps or withdrawals. EXIT CRITERIA: Trace all state changes affecting reserves, balances, pricing formulas, LP supply, and redemption outputs; identify every caller and dependent pricing path; determine whether same-transaction manipulation is possible and whether any invariant, oracle, minimum-output, or synchronization control prevents exploitation; document a concrete exploit path or conclude that price manipulation is adequately bounded.

frame_6364bb0ac887.question: Vulnerability analysis of DaoVault
artifact_refs: Spot-price-dependent LP valuation and weight recalculation
Deposit, harvest, and withdrawal accounting that can be influenced by pool reserves
Whether temporary AMM price manipulation enables disproportionate vault shares, rewards, or withdrawals

history.rationale: WHY NOW: DaoVault is an unvisited major component explicitly annotated as using spot-valued weights and recalculating weight on deposit, while Pool has already established mutable spot pricing as a confirmed price-manipulation risk. This makes DaoVault a high-priority downstream consumer that may convert a transient pool price distortion into persistent share, reward, or redemption value. EXIT CRITERIA: Trace all DaoVault valuation and weight calculations through deposit, harvest, and withdrawal; identify every price/reserve source and whether it is manipulable within the same transaction or surrounding transactions; verify whether share issuance, rewards, or LP redemption can be profitably distorted; conclude with either a concrete exploit path and affected state or documented evidence that manipulation is bounded or independently protected.

frame_942b4e0c2d41.question: Vulnerability analysis of BASE / SPARTA token
artifact_refs: Transfer-fee and burn behavior affecting pool balance-delta accounting
Minting, burning, and transferAndCall paths that can alter AMM reserves or spot prices
Whether token supply or balance changes enable price manipulation before oracle-dependent actions

history.rationale: WHY NOW: This unvisited token component directly affects balances used by Pool reserve and swap pricing, while existing hypotheses identify spot-price manipulation as a high-priority risk. Its transfer fee, burn, and callback semantics may create balance/reserve discrepancies that can be exploited to distort prices or influence downstream spot-valued calculations. EXIT CRITERIA: Trace every externally reachable mint, burn, transfer, and transferAndCall path; map effects on pool balances and recorded reserves; identify whether an attacker can create a profitable price distortion or bypass expected reserve accounting; conclude with either a concrete price-manipulation finding and affected flows or documented evidence that these token operations cannot materially influence pricing.

frame_e134e18cc97a.question: Vulnerability analysis of SynthFactory token-to-synth and isSynth registries
artifact_refs: Whether token-to-synth mappings can be manipulated to redirect synth pricing or valuation
Whether isSynth classification can be forged, stale, duplicated, or inconsistently cleared
Whether registry lookups used by swaps, vaults, or pricing paths accept attacker-controlled synth identities

history.rationale: WHY NOW: This is the remaining non-interface component and directly controls asset identity used by synth-related pricing and swap paths. A manipulated or inconsistent registry could cause protocols to treat an attacker-selected token as a valid synth or resolve the wrong synth for valuation. EXIT CRITERIA: Trace every write and read of token-to-synth and isSynth state, identify all callers that use these values in price-sensitive calculations or asset routing, and determine whether any permissionless or stale mapping can alter a victim's effective price or synth valuation. Stop when all registry mutation and consumption paths are covered with no exploitable price impact found.
